title: Doc2Harness: Benchmarking LLMs on Long-Horizon Harness Engineering of Coding Agents
snippet: Agents driven by large language models are increasingly deployed on long-horizon tasks, where they use tools and modify real workspaces. How well they perform depends as much on the harness around the model as on the model itself. Existing benchmarks measure downstream task success under a fixed harness, leaving harness engineering itself unexplored. We propose Doc2Harness, a two-stage benchmark that evaluates long-horizon harness engineering directly. In Stage 1, a build model operating inside a fixed builder harness receives an interface-only contract skeleton and a development document tha…
summary: Doc2Harness is a benchmark that measures how well LLMs build the harness around coding agents for long-horizon tasks.
whyItMatters: Highlights that the surrounding harness, not just the model, drives agent performance.

title: Recovering Reliable Supervision via Critique-Guided On-Policy Distillation
snippet: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student model on its own rollouts with token-level supervision from a teacher, assuming that the teacher can reach a correct answer from any prefix the student writes. We call this property the recoverability of the teacher and show it fails on incorrect rollouts: the teacher follows student errors, although it recognizes them. We propose CriticOPD, using error recognition to restore recoverability. The teacher critiques an incorrect rollout, allowing the student to rewrite its solution following the error. The resulting output, including the critique as …
summary: CriticOPD has the teacher critique incorrect student rollouts so the student can rewrite them, addressing failures of on-policy distillation.
whyItMatters: A practical fix for distillation signals that teachers otherwise follow student errors.

title: RuleTrek: Benchmarking Agentic Rule Reasoning in Complex Scenarios
snippet: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly tackle complex real-world tasks in specialized domains. However, identifying and correctly applying domain-specific rules remains challenging when scenario information is distributed across multiple files. Existing rule-reasoning benchmarks typically represent scenarios using only a few factual statements, simplifying the identification and application of relevant rules. To address this gap, this paper introduces RuleTrek, a multi-domain benchmark for agentic rule reasoning in complex scenarios. Its rule-grounded construction pipeline extracts structu…
summary: RuleTrek is a benchmark testing whether LLM agents can find and apply domain rules when scenario facts are spread across multiple files.
whyItMatters: Exposes a realistic weakness in agents working over document-heavy domains.

Addressing this challenge requires effective memory mechanisms that can maintain continuity across sessions, adapt to changing users and environments, and refine memory-management policies through accu…
